diagnosis: The automation profile execution endpoint launches a persistent Playwright browser context using profile.user_data_dir and evaluates user-provided JavaScript in the target page. It looks up the profile by profile_id but omits checking if profile.owner_tenant_id matches user.tenant_id. An attacker can dispatch actions within another tenant's authenticated browser profile to perform unauthorized transactions.

corrected_code:
from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException, status
from pydantic import BaseModel
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

router = APIRouter(prefix="/automation/profiles")

class WorkflowExecutionRequest(BaseModel):
    target_url: str
    action_script: str

@router.post("/{profile_id}/dispatch-workflow")
async def dispatch_profile_workflow(
    profile_id: str,
    payload: WorkflowExecutionRequest,
    profile_store: BrowserProfileStore = Depends(get_profile_store),
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user)
):
    profile = await profile_store.find_profile(profile_id)
    if not profile:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_404_NOT_FOUND, detail="Browser profile not found")

    if profile.owner_tenant_id != user.tenant_id:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_403_FORBIDDEN, detail="Profile does not belong to your organization")

    async with async_playwright() as p:
        context = await p.chromium.launch_persistent_context(
            user_data_dir=profile.user_data_dir,
            headless=True
        )
        page = await context.new_page()
        await page.goto(payload.target_url)
        result = await page.evaluate(payload.action_script)
        await context.close()

    return {"status": "executed", "profile_id": profile_id, "result": result}
